This tick applies the same pattern to PaymentMeans/PayeeFinancialAccount (model/charges.py), the cluster's next already-modeled component family.

inputs.acceptance_evidence: 8 new tests prove validate() now also detects cardinality violations for cac:PaymentMeans's PaymentMeansCode/PaymentDueDate/PayeeFinancialAccount fields and cac:PayeeFinancialAccount's ID/Name/CurrencyCode fields, while correctly never flagging PaymentMeans.PaymentID (genuinely minOccurs=0 maxOccurs=UNBOUNDED per the schema, unlike its sibling fields), proven as its own dedicated test rather than assumed uniform with the other fields.

execution_steps: 1. Read model/charges.py's PaymentMeans and FinancialAccount dataclasses directly: PaymentMeans models payment_means_code/payment_due_date/payment_id/payee_financial_account; FinancialAccount models id/name/currency_code, projected from the cac:PayeeFinancialAccount element specifically (not a generic cac:FinancialAccount -- confirmed by reading financial_account_of's caller, payment_means_of, which calls find(node, 'PayeeFinancialAccount')).

2. Extracted PaymentMeansType's and FinancialAccountType's complete field lists with exact minOccurs/maxOccurs directly from the pinned OASIS UBL 2.3 release ZIP (same source as event 216's Party/PostalAddress/Contact work). Found a genuine discrepancy worth documenting rather than silently working around: PaymentMeansType declares cbc:PaymentID as minOccurs=0 maxOccurs=UNBOUNDED (repeatable), even though this package's own PaymentMeans.payment_id field models only a single value -- deliberately excluded PaymentID from the new cardinality check rather than either flagging legitimately-repeated instances as violations or silently fixing the separate model-scoping question, which is out of scope for a validation-only tick.

3. Refactored _cardinality_diagnostics() from a growing if/elif chain into a qname-keyed dict (_CARDINALITY_CHECKED_COMPONENTS), making it straightforward to extend with more already-modeled components in future ticks without the function itself growing unboundedly.

4. Verified interactively before writing formal tests: a single PaymentMeansCode validates cleanly; two PaymentMeansCode/PaymentDueDate/PayeeFinancialAccount values are each flagged; multiple PaymentID values are correctly NOT flagged; two CurrencyCode values inside PayeeFinancialAccount are flagged -- all 5 cases correct on the first attempt.
5. Ran the full pre-existing ubl suite (896 tests, zero new fixtures) against the extended check to look for false positives before writing a single new test -- all 896 passed unchanged.

6. Wrote 8 formal tests mirroring event 216's structure: positive/negative cases for each newly-checked field, plus a dedicated test proving PaymentID's genuine repeatability is honored, not accidentally flagged. Ran ruff (clean), the full ubl suite (904 passed, was 896, +8), and the full 6-format regression (3270 passed, was 3262, +8; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.
